events.title: Li Shimin kills his brothers in the Xuanwu Gate Incident
events.description: Prince Li Shimin ambushed and killed his brothers Li Jiancheng and Li Yuanji at the Xuanwu Gate of Chang'an. Within two months his father abdicated, and as Emperor Taizong he presided over a golden age of Tang China.

events.title: Continental Congress votes for independence from Britain
events.description: Congress adopted the Lee Resolution declaring the colonies free and independent states, with twelve in favour and New York abstaining. John Adams predicted that 2 July would be celebrated for ever; posterity chose the 4th.
events.html: Congress adopted the Lee Resolution declaring the colonies free and independent states, with twelve in favour and New York abstaining. John Adams predicted that 2 July would be celebrated for ever; posterity chose the 4th.

events.title: Union troops hold Little Round Top on Gettysburg's second day
events.description: Confederate assaults struck the Union left at Little Round Top, the Wheatfield and the Peach Orchard. The Union line held its high ground by a narrow margin, setting the stage for Pickett's Charge the next day.

events.title: First Zeppelin airship flies over Lake Constance
events.description: Count Ferdinand von Zeppelin's LZ 1 made its maiden flight from a floating hangar on Lake Constance. It was the first flight of a rigid airship, beginning an era that ended with the Hindenburg disaster of 1937.
events.html: Count Ferdinand von Zeppelin's LZ 1 made its maiden flight from a floating hangar on Lake Constance. It was the first flight of a rigid airship, beginning an era that ended with the Hindenburg disaster of 1937.

events.title: Amelia Earhart disappears over the Pacific
events.description: Amelia Earhart and navigator Fred Noonan vanished while searching for tiny Howland Island on the last long legs of their round-the-world flight. Despite a vast search, their fate has never been conclusively established.

events.title: Lyndon Johnson signs the Civil Rights Act
events.description: President Johnson signed the Civil Rights Act, outlawing discrimination on the basis of race, colour, religion, sex or national origin. It ended legal segregation in public places and was the most sweeping civil rights law since Reconstruction.
